Home/Growth Lab/Trial-to-paid conversion rate

Product / Onboarding and conversion

Trial-to-paid conversion rate

The share of unique trial accounts in a defined trial-start cohort that become paying accounts by a stated deadline, such as 30 days after trial start. The deadline must allow each included trial the same opportunity to convert.

Explore in the metric hierarchy ↗Open calculators →
Level 4Inspect the detail

The share of unique trial accounts in a defined trial-start cohort that become paying accounts by a stated deadline, such as 30 days after trial start. The deadline must allow each included trial the same opportunity to convert.

%

How we use it

We combine activation, product usage, and purchase events to assess which onboarding experiences produce customers rather than trial volume alone.

Transparent calculationTrial-cohort accounts becoming paying by the deadline ÷ eligible unique trial accounts in that cohort × 100
eligible trial accounts250
converted trial accounts50

50 ÷ 250 × 100 = 20% trial-to-paid conversion within the agreed window.

Illustrative calculation. Not a client result or a universal benchmark.

Break the result down

  • Trial start cohort
  • Plan and acquisition source
  • Trial experience and sales support

Questions we investigate

  • Are paid conversions linked to eligible trial accounts?
  • Where do users fail to experience value?
  • Do trial length and follow-up differ across cohorts?

Actions the evidence supports

  • Reconcile trial accounts with first payments.
  • Improve relevant trial onboarding and follow-up.
  • Compare like-for-like eligibility and conversion windows.

Reporting contract

Ownership & cadence

Product growth and sales leads
Weekly or monthly after conversion deadlines mature.

Required data

  • Unique eligible trial account cohort
  • First-payment events linked to trial accounts
  • Trial deadline, plan, and exclusion policy

Read the measure with context

Zero eligible trials makes the rate undefined. Immature trials bias the result downward. Define successful payment, trial extensions, duplicate trials, and opt-in versus automatic billing. This is a trial-cohort measure rather than paid accounts divided by all active users.
